Governors
The School Governors
The School Governors play a very active role in our school. The governing body consists of thirteen governors, including parents, staff, Local Authority (LA) and community representatives.
The Governing Body of Juniper Hill School sets a clear strategic direction to secure a high-quality, ambitious and inclusive education for every pupil. We are committed to ensuring that all learners, particularly the most vulnerable, feel valued, are supported to succeed, and are able to flourish through a broad and enriching curriculum. Through strong accountability and effective stewardship of resources, we drive continuous improvement and ensure the best possible outcomes for all.
The Full Governing Board meets once a term. Its core responsibilities are:
1. Provide strategic leadership Set and monitor the school’s vision, values and strategic priorities to ensure long-term improvement.
2. Ensure a high quality, inclusive curriculum Hold leaders to account for delivering an ambitious curriculum that meets the needs of all pupils, including the most vulnerable, and enables them to make strong progress.
3. Oversee financial performance and resources Ensure the school’s budget, staffing and resources are used effectively, provide value for money, and support the school development plan, including the maintenance and improvement of the school environment.
4. Hold the school to account for educational performance Monitor and evaluate pupil outcomes, teaching quality, behaviour, attendance and safeguarding to ensure high standards and continuous improvement.
We have three subcommittees that each focus on delivering against one of the core responsibilities. These committees each meet once a term:
1. The Strategy and Planning (S&P) committee includes all governors and is concerned with the management of annual and long-term planning processes.
2. The Teaching, Learning and Community (TL&C) committee focusses on pupils’ learning and behaviour and the school’s links with the wider community.
3. The Finance and Resources (F&R) committee oversees the finances and premises (including health and safety) of the school.
Additionally, there is a separate Pay Sub-committee to ensure we meet our statutory responsibility to consider and approve the Pay Policy annually.
Self-evaluation is a vital part of our culture here at Juniper Hill. We have a formal process of constantly reviewing all aspects of the school and we listen to everyone involved for their ideas. We have a “School Plan” of priority actions that each subcommittee of the governing body decides are necessary to address areas where we want to develop further, focusing mainly on curriculum areas and the development of the school premises. In the last ten years, we have built new classrooms and a new library, refurbished all the toilets and the kitchen, and created a splendid adventure playground. Funding for these projects has been raised using our annual capital grants and extensive support from the Juniper Hill PTA.
Minutes of the meetings of the Governing Body are available in school. Key policies can be found on the 'Policies' page on the 'Parents' tab. If you would like to know any more about the school governors or are interested in getting involved, please contact any of the following governors or ask in the school office.

A group of Governors may be required to form the Complaints Panel, Staff Dismissal, Staff Dismissal Appeals, Employee Grievance, Pay Review Appeals or Pupil Discipline Committees. The Chair of Governors has the authority to form such committees from the Governor’s pool, should they be required to meet, and a Chair of such a committee would be elected at such a meeting. No Governor can sit on a committee if they have prior knowledge of a staff dismissal incident, an employee grievance, an exclusion issue or staff (with regard to pay related issues). Any Governor who sits on the Staff Dismissal committee cannot sit on the Staff Dismissal Appeals committee.
Many of our Policies are available online as pdf documents – please click on the 'Policies' page under the 'Parents' section of the website.
Other documents are available on request from the school office. There is a file readily available in the school reception area of the Minutes of the termly Full Governing Body Meetings, and other committee minutes and documents are filed by the office. Single copies of most items are free. If your request means that we have to do a lot of photocopying or printing, or pay a large postage charge, or is for a priced item such as some printed publications or videos, we will let you know the cost before fulfilling your request.
Juniper Hill School is committed to the highest standards of ethical governance, transparency, and public accountability. In line with the Nolan Principles of Public Life, the Governing Board proactively manages all actual and perceived conflicts of interest to protect the integrity of its decision‑making.
Three members of the Governing Board have close personal relationships with members of school staff. These interests have been formally declared and are managed in accordance with statutory guidance and the school’s governance protocols. The Governing Board has put in place clear and consistent safeguards to ensure impartiality and maintain public confidence.
These measures ensure that any potential for bias, real or perceived, is fully mitigated and that governance decisions remain objective and transparent.

pageCache.text:
Behaviour and the power of relationships
At Juniper Hill School, we believe that positive behaviour and positive relationships are intrinsically connected. Children need to feel adults around them, like them, care about them and are interested in them.
Through our Relational Policy, we have created a culture where we aim for every child to feel safe, respected, valued and understood, enabling them to thrive both socially and academically. We have high aspirations for every child and recognise that strong relationships, with their friends and the Juniper Team are the foundation for successful learning and personal development.
Through our Behaviour Curriculum, we explicitly teach the behaviours and life skills children need to succeed, including learning behaviours, cooperation, kindness, respect, good manners and responsibility. Kagan Cooperative Learning structures, used in all classes across the school provide regular opportunities for children to practise these skills, helping them develop teamwork, confidence at talking to others, sharing their views, and listening skills.
By combining clear expectations with warm, rich relationships and consistent support, we create a calm, inclusive and purposeful environment where every child can learn, contribute and achieve their very best.

PE and Sports Premium
​​​​The Sports Premium is a government fund given to primary schools to help improve the quality of physical education, sport, and physical activity. It enables schools to provide wider opportunities such as specialist coaching, new equipment, and a broader range of clubs and activities.
At Juniper Hill, we value sports. We are highly committed to developing a lifelong love of sport and physical activity for all of our children. We teach children regular exercise not only supports physical development but also plays a vital role in boosting their wellbeing, confidence, and readiness to learn. Through high-quality PE and inclusive sporting opportunities, we aim to help every child feel healthy, motivated, and proud of their sporting achievements.

pageCache.text:
Universal Provision / SEND / SEMH Unit
Inclusion Strategy
Juniper Hill's inclusion strategy is underpinned by statutory guidance, including the Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) Code of Practice: 0–25 years (2015) and the Children and Families Act (2014). These frameworks establish the expectation that all children and young people, regardless of need, are entitled to a broad, balanced, and inclusive education where barriers to learning are identified and addressed effectively.
In alignment with this, our approach to inclusion reflects our school values. We aspire for ALL children to enjoy coming to school and feel they belong in our Juniper Community, they are successful and achieve their best and thrive. We believe that:
Our inclusive culture ensures that SEND provision is embedded in everyday teaching and learning. Through high-quality teaching, early identification, and a graduated approach to support, we ensure that pupils with SEND can access the curriculum, participate fully in school life, and make excellent progress.
High expectations apply to all learners.
Universal Provision
Universal Provision at Juniper Hill School is inclusive, high-quality classroom practice that ensures all pupils receive clear, structured, and engaging learning experiences through carefully planned lessons and effective pedagogy.
Teaching at Juniper, is underpinned by Rosenshine’s principles:
reviewing prior learning
presenting new material in small steps
using guided practice
checking for understanding
providing regular opportunities for independent practice.
This approach supports ALL learners.
This supports pupils in building knowledge, confidence, and long-term retention of learning.
Collaborative learning is strengthened through Kagan cooperative structures which promote:
Positive interdependence
Individual accountability
Simultaneous interaction
Through consistent routines, adaptive teaching, and purposeful cooperative learning opportunities, universal provision enables every child to feel supported, challenged, and successful within an ambitious and inclusive curriculum.
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
We work in partnership with the Local Authority to support any child who has an EHCP (Education, Health and Care Plan). If a child already has an EHCP or has significant special or medical needs, please talk to us in confidence so that together we can ensure that all aspects of the admission process take place in good time, to ensure the best support for your child. All teaching is carefully planned so the needs of all pupils are met. Lessons are adapted to ensure all children are supported and challenged. Pupils with significant special educational needs will have individual programmes / interventions, to address the targets on their EHCP, as well as adult support when necessary.
In Autumn 2024, we opened an SEMH Unit (The Nest) at Juniper Hill School. The Nest provides an environment rich in support, nurture and therapeutic interventions for 12 children aged 4-11 years who have experienced disrupted childhoods ACE’s (adverse childhood experiences). Many of the children who join us are in in foster care/adopted/special guardianship etc.
Children who have suffered adverse childhood experiences can find the demands of school life difficult and are more likely to experience challenges as young people.
Juniper Hill School’s motto of Kindness, Enjoyment and Achievement is at the heart of all we do. Juniper is an attachment aware trauma informed school.
The Nest are taught a bespoke curriculum, with regulation opportunities embedded as part of each child's individual week plan. We provide warm, rich, positive relational experiences in our beautiful environment. We work alongside our families to do the best we can to meet our children’s individual, learning and attachment needs.
Our Nest Team consists of a specialist Lead Teacher, trained LSA’s, and Speech and Language Therapist (1-day a week).
‘Children who have experienced trauma need to be in an environment where they feel safe, seen, soothed and secure.’ Louise Bomber.
Safe: We aim to provide a physically and emotionally safe environment. Trust and respect will be fostered, consistent routines established, clear boundaries and high expectations set.
Seen: Children will be truly understood and acknowledged (seen) through active listening, empathy and recognition of each child’s unique needs and strengths.
Soothed: We will help children to regulate their emotions, to provide comfort, gentle words, sensory experiences and reassurance and a calm approach when they are feeling distressed.
Secure: Children will feel secure through positive relationships with adults who are emotionally available and responsive to them. We will provide a stable and predictable environment. Security allows children to be able to explore the world and learn without fear.
We delight in our children
We are proud of the fact that our school has a positive attitude towards the inclusion of all pupils as we wish our school to be a true reflection of the society in which our children live.
Mrs Lauren Long is our Assistant Head for Inclusion / SENDCo, can be contacted via the school office on 01628 523536.

Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club
At Juniper Hill School we offer a Breakfast Club from 7.45am to 8.45am when school starts. Each session costs £6.00 per child and includes a choice of cereal, toast, milk, fruit and fruit juice. Children are supervised by our experienced team and there are a range of activities to choose from. At 8.45am the children are taken to the playground prior to going into class for registration.
Booking of places and payment for Breakfast Club is done via the School Shop on Parentmail PMX. Once your child has been admitted to school and your details have been entered onto Parentmail, you will receive an email inviting you to set up your account and password. Please contact the school office if you have any difficulties accessing Parentmail or the School Shop.
Breakfast Club can be booked for a whole term if you wish, or on a week by week basis. You are able to make bookings up until 12.00pm Friday for the following week.
Our Breakfast Club is proving to be very popular with parents and children alike and we are delighted to be able to offer this service to our school community.
If you would like to pay for Breakfast Club with childcare vouchers or tax-free childcare please contact the school office for further information.

pageCache.text:
Extra-Curricular
After School Sports and other Activities
The school promotes a wide range of extra-curricular activities at lunchtimes and after school. Some of these are provided by our own staff and some are provided by external agencies at an additional cost. The following are some of the activities that may take place during the school year, depending on the skills and enthusiasms of our staff. These are often targeted at particular age groups of children.
Football, Netball, Athletics, Cycling, Hockey, Basketball, Table Tennis, Cricket.
Art, Cookery, Orchard Club, Choir, Drama, Sewing.
All children have the opportunity to learn to play a musical instrument from Year 2 upwards, depending on the instrument. Our team of very experienced peripatetic music teachers provide lessons for a wide variety of instruments. Currently these include guitar, woodwind, recorder, piano and drums. Charges are made for these lessons. In addition the children have the opportunity to perform at our annual music concert each summer. On several occasions our children have also performed at The Royal Albert Hall and at the O2.
Visitors to our school include members of our local community, theatre groups, history experts, cricket and badminton coaches and First Soccer.

Diversity Statement
The governors believe it is important that boards reflect the diversity of the school communities they serve. Diverse boards promote inclusive school environments and provide diverse role models for staff and young people.
The governors currently monitor data on the diversity of the board, including data on age, gender, and ethnicity. They will use that data to inform their recruitment and training needs and ensure there is always a diverse range of perspectives around the table to support robust decision-making.
Due to our relatively small governing board, we will not publish the diversity data online as individual governors could be identified and we have a legal obligation to protect their personal data.

External Reports
Juniper Hill is a restless, reflective school. We value learning from external agencies.
We are members of Challenge Partners.
Challenge Partners is a national network of schools and trusts working together to improve education for all children. It brings schools into a collaborative partnership where they share expertise, learn from one another, and take part in supportive peer reviews to strengthen teaching, leadership, and outcomes.
Part of our membership allows us to engage in a Quality Assurance Review (QAR). This is a rigorous, three-day peer evaluation carried out by trained senior leaders from other schools. The programme helps us to identify strengths, address areas, and develop and share effective practice across the partnership.
In our 2024 QAR we were awarded an area of excellence in co-operative learning.
In our 2025 QAR we achieved Leading and were awarded an area of excellent in inclusion.
In our 2026 QAR we achieved Leading and were awarded an area of excellent in writing.
We value our relationship with Challenge Partners and the access to high-quality professional development and leadership growth opportunities it provides.
Juniper Hill School was last inspected in July 2022. We are proud of the progress we have made since our last inspection. Our next inspection will take place under the new Ofsted framework.

Home School Agreement
A Home School Agreement is a statement explaining the school's responsibilities towards its pupils, the responsibilities of the pupil's families, and what's expected of pupils.
At Juniper Hill School we want our children to thrive. We believe a close partnership between the school; our families and our children are at the heart of enabling our children to benefit from the best primary school experience we can offer.
We ask all families and children to confirm they have read our home-school agreement at the start of every academic year.
